correctness.rationale: Parseval for (a+bz+cz²)^4 gives nine Fourier coefficients. I independently expanded the exact eighth-moment polynomial in A=|a|²+|c|², B=|b|², R=|ac| under aligned phases and verified all thirteen monomials in the displayed identity. Each R coefficient is nonnegative and the nonzero-variable derivative strictly positive, so for fixed A,B equality forces endpoint magnitudes equal, R=A/2. A two-term boundary has at most (8 choose 4)/16=35/8, below the interior candidate. The one-variable ratio Ψ(t)=(70t⁴+560t³+420t²+56t+1)/(1+2t)^4 has Ψ′=−24(35t³−21t−2)/(1+2t)^5, with a unique positive root and global maximum, giving K8^8=13.787723967226... and all phases satisfying arg a+arg c−2arg b=0. Independent symbolic resultant equals 891 times the claimed cubic in K8^8; exact factor and root cases checked analytically.

Deriving a rigid nontrivial amplitude ratio is more than a routine Parseval identity or table recomputation; the precise equality class is independently useful in finite-dimensional Fourier optimization.
